public: On 21 December 2023, the Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2719 at meeting S/PV.9518 on financing for African Union-led peace support operations.
The Council agreed to consider requests from the African Union Peace and Security Council case by case. Authorized operations would remain under African Union command and control.

For operations authorized by the Council, UN assessed contributions may cover up to 75 percent of the annual operation budget. The UN and African Union are to jointly mobilize the remainder as extrabudgetary resources. The Council committed to consider viable options if significant shortfalls arise.

cards.speaker: Procedural officer
cards.source: At S/PV.9518, the Council voted on the US amendment S/2023/1023 before the final draft. The amendment was adopted with nine votes in favour, none against and six abstentions, including France. The amended draft S/2023/999 then passed unanimously with 15 votes in favour (S/PV.9518, pp. 3–4; Repertoire Table 16).

cards.speaker: United States
cards.source: The United States said it read the draft's reference to an appropriate amount as excluding full UN financing, but called for an explicit contribution limit to remove ambiguity and help enable timely deployment. It submitted S/2023/1023 and urged support for the amendment (S/PV.9518, p. 3).

cards.speaker: France
cards.source: France was unable to support the US amendment because it did not see enough clarity and predictability about financing the 25 percent outside assessed contributions. France reaffirmed support for assessed UN financing for AU-led operations and was prepared to discuss different contribution levels from the UN and EU (S/PV.9518, p. 4).

criteria.instruction: Attribute S/2023/1023 to the United States, give the 9–0–6 amendment result, and distinguish it from the subsequent unanimous final vote.
Attribute to the US the view that the original wording excluded full UN financing, and the rationale that an explicit cap would remove ambiguity and support timely deployment.

Attribute to France concern over insufficiently clear, predictable funding outside assessed contributions, preserve its support for assessed financing and readiness to discuss UN and EU contribution levels.
Explicitly reconcile France's amendment abstention with its vote for the amended resolution, with evidence for both votes and its finance concern.

Explain how the US amendment was adopted despite France's reservation, explicitly distinguish the US desire for a clear assessed ceiling from France's concern about the remainder, and avoid suggesting either the cap or the remainder was rejected.
